name: Hypertrophic or Verrucous Lupus Erythematosus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Presence of hypertrophic, verrucous, hyperkeratotic plaques predominantly on sun-exposed skin
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with interface dermatitis, basal cell degeneration, and thickened basement membrane
Direct immunofluorescence demonstrating granular deposition of IgG, IgM, and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction
Presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) or other lupus-specific autoantibodies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical clinical lesions plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, histological, and immunopathological findings; serology may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically located on sun-exposed areas such as the face and extensor surfaces

pathognomonic.symptomName: Erythematous indurated plaques with adherent scale

searchTerms: skin lesions worsen with sun exposure

common.symptomName: Scarring and atrophy following lesion resolution
searchTerms: scars and thinning skin after rash heals

common.symptomName: Hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation in chronic lesions
searchTerms: dark or light skin patches in chronic lesions
uneven skin pigmentation in affected areas

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain or tenderness over plaques

searchTerms: swollen lymph nodes near skin lesions
enlarged lymph nodes by affected skin

occasional.symptomName: Mild systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: slight systemic symptoms like mild fever

occasional.symptomName: Nail changes including ridging or pitting

rare.symptomName: Development of squamous cell carcinoma within chronic lesions
rare.notes: Malignant transformation is rare but documented
searchTerms: skin cancer developing in chronic lesions
squamous cell carcinoma in long-term skin patches
deep skin inflammation involving fat layer
subcutaneous fat inflammation under skin lesions

rare.symptomName: Arthralgia or arthritis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus
searchTerms: joint pain or swelling with lupus

laboratory: Positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in 30-50% of cases
Elevated anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies in some patients
Mild leukopenia or anemia may be present
imaging: Not routinely required; imaging may be used to exclude deeper tissue involvement
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; association with HLA-DR2 and HLA-DR3 alleles reported in lupus erythematosus
other: Direct immunofluorescence showing granular IgG, IgM, and C3 deposits at dermoepidermal junction
Histopathology demonstrating epidermal hyperplasia with interface dermatitis and basement membrane thickening

distinguishingFeatures: Regular acanthosis with elongation of rete ridges on histology
Absence of lupus band on immunofluorescence

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or ulceration of lesions suggesting malignant transformation
Development of systemic lupus erythematosus symptoms (e.g., arthritis, nephritis)
references: Kuhn A, et al. Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus: Clinical Features, Pathogenesis, and Treatment. Dermatol Clin. 2019;37(4):365-379.
Werth VP. Clinical manifestations of cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Autoimmunity. 2005;38(1):5-9.
